direct_answer:
BASF integrates sustainability-related performance into incentives primarily through climate and other sustainability targets in variable remuneration for the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives, while Supervisory Board remuneration is not linked to sustainability because it has no variable components [Source 1].

- Long-term incentive (LTI): Reducing Group-wide CO2 emissions (Scope 1 and Scope 2) is anchored as “the most important nonfinancial key performance indicator” in BASF’s steering and compensation systems (since 2020) and is “one of three equally weighted (33.3%) strategic targets” for the LTI of the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives [Source 1].
- Short-term incentive (STI) for senior executives in operating business units: In the reporting year, BASF introduced an STI program with three additional (non-financial) targets alongside financial targets: (i) occupational and process safety, (ii) sustainability, and (iii) development of the operating divisions [Source 1]. The first two are sustainability-related [Source 1]. These three objectives are equally weighted in the STI calculation and together account for 25% of the total STI formula; therefore, 16.7% of the entire STI formula is sustainability-related [Source 1]. The sustainability target includes elements supporting BASF’s “green transformation,” such as sales of Sustainable-Future Solutions and increasing the share of purchased raw materials with supplier-specific Product Carbon Footprints [Source 1].
- Supervisory Board: Supervisory Board remuneration “does not include any variable components and so is not linked to target achievement” (including sustainability targets) [Source 1].

The retrieved passages do not specify the governance level at which the incentive scheme terms are approved and updated (e.g., which body approves/updates LTI/STI sustainability metrics) [Source 1].
compliance_rationale: The evidence describes key characteristics of the incentive schemes (LTI and STI), identifies specific sustainability-related targets/metrics (Scope 1&2 CO2 reduction; occupational/process safety; sustainability elements such as Sustainable-Future Solutions sales and supplier-specific PCFs), and quantifies the proportion of variable remuneration linked to sustainability for both LTI (33.3% of LTI) and STI (16.7% of STI formula) [Source 1]. However, the passages do not provide the required information on the level at which the terms of the incentive schemes are approved and updated, and do not fully detail how sustainability metrics are embedded as benchmarks beyond the described weightings and target elements [Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: Approval and update governance: the level/body in the undertaking at which the terms of the incentive schemes are approved and updated is not stated in the retrieved passages [Source 1].

Administrative bodies coverage: the passages explicitly cover the Board of Executive Directors, senior executives, and the Supervisory Board, but do not clarify whether any other administrative/management body members beyond these groups are covered by sustainability-linked incentives [Source 1].

Further detail on performance assessment mechanics: the passages name targets and weightings but do not explain measurement methodology, thresholds, or payout curves for the sustainability targets within LTI/STI [Source 1].
key_findings: Scope 1 and Scope 2 CO2 emissions reduction is the most important nonfinancial KPI in BASF’s steering and compensation systems and is weighted 33.3% in the LTI for the Board of Executive Directors and senior executives [Source 1].
Supervisory Board remuneration has no variable component and is therefore not linked to sustainability target achievement [Source 1].

An STI program for senior executives in operating business units includes sustainability-related targets (occupational/process safety and sustainability) with sustainability-related components totaling 16.7% of the STI formula [Source 1].

The STI sustainability target includes elements such as sales of Sustainable-Future Solutions and increasing the share of purchased raw materials with supplier-specific Product Carbon Footprints [Source 1].
